title: Unit Composition
description: Describes the internal model-type breakdown of a unit.

faction_id.description: Owning faction. A chassis shared across factions has a distinct composition per faction under the same `unit_id`, so compositions are keyed by (faction_id, unit_id).

default_weapon_ids.description: The model's no-choice equipment multiset, used by base_loadout. It must describe a legal default configuration even when whole-model variants are present; it does not implicitly add another selectable variant.

excluded_from_enhancements.description: True when this model cannot be given an Enhancement even though it is a CHARACTER (e.g. Ogryn Bodyguard, Transcendent C'tan). An Enhancement needs a model in the unit that is not excluded.

base_size_mm.description: This model's base. Absent when no base could be resolved for the model.

hull_shape_id.description: Optional reference to a hull-shape entity giving this model's 2D collision polygon, used instead of the circular/oval base footprint. By convention a model carrying this should set `base_size_mm.shape` to "hull".

loadout_variants.description: Mutually exclusive whole-model loadout alternatives, expressed as named peers rather than deltas against default_weapon_ids. Each selected variant supplies one model's complete initial equipment multiset; repeated IDs preserve multiplicity. Compatible item-level wargear_options may transform that loadout but must satisfy the resulting variant's selection limits and all equipment budgets. When absent, models start with default_weapon_ids. When present, default_weapon_ids still governs base_loadout and is not replaced.

name.description: The source peer's own model name (e.g. "Boy w/ Big shoota"). Unique within this model row.

weapon_ids.description: This variant's complete per-model equipment multiset. Every ID must be in the owning unit's weapon_ids or resolve to faction wargear. Repeated IDs mean multiple copies; an empty multiset is not a loadout.

max_count.description: Ceiling on how many models of this row may take this variant, when the source states one on the variant itself. Shared and ratio-scaled ceilings live in `loadout_variant_budgets` instead.

loadout_variant_budgets.description: Caps over how many variant selections this model row may make, counting SELECTED VARIANTS rather than final weapon ids (two variants sharing a weapon must not charge each other's allowance). A singleton `variant_names` is an individual cap, several names a shared pool, and intersecting budgets a ratio plus a hard ceiling. The selected count across `variant_names` must not exceed `floor(scope_model_count * count / per_models)`, `count * floor(scope_model_count / per_models)` when `stepped`, or simply `count` when `per_models` is 0.

variant_names.description: The `loadout_variants[].name` values sharing this allowance. Every name must exist in this same model row.

per_models.description: Models required per `count` selections. 0 means the flat limit `count`, independent of squad size.

scope.description: Which model count scales the allowance: the whole unit, or just this model row.

stepped.description: When true, the allowance grows only per full block of `per_models` models: `count * floor(scope_model_count / per_models)` ("for every 5 models, up to 2" is 2 at 5-9 models and 4 at 10). Absent or false, it is the proportional `floor(scope_model_count * count / per_models)`. Meaningless when `per_models` is 0.

tiers.description: The discrete buildable squad sizes (GW's per-datasheet unit-composition rows). Each tier gives a per-model count range; a legal squad must match exactly one tier. When absent, the squad is treated as a single implicit tier equal to `models[]`. The top-level `models[]` min/max are the aggregate envelope (min-of-mins / max-of-maxes) across the tiers, so consumers that read only `models[]` still see the full range.

models.description: One entry per top-level `models[]` row, matched by `name`, giving this tier's count range for that model type.

loadout.description: The unit's wargear rules in the structure of GW's Munitorum Field Manual data, keyed by repo item ids and model names; a name several rows of `models` share is written `name#k` for the k-th of them. Each model makes `picks` choices from every slot on its model row (or takes its alternate slot instead of all of them); limits cap the unit's choices; uniform sets make every model on a row carry the same main option. Absent for units the MFM does not cover.

stock.description: The default unit: for each model row, its model count and the unit-wide copies of each item. A row without `model` holds wargear the unit takes once.

individual.description: The app lists this row's models one by one, each with its own widgets, so a checkbox on the row is one per model rather than one for the row.

templates.description: What one model of a row carries when added beyond the default unit.

slots.description: Per-model choice menus. A model's wargear is the union of its picks across its row's slots.

model.description: The model row the slot belongs to; absent for a slot the unit fills once.

picks.description: Choices each model makes from this slot.

repeats.description: Whether one choice can be picked more than once.

alternate.description: A model takes this slot instead of every non-alternate slot on its row.

limits.description: Caps on how many of a set of choices the unit may take, counted on the unit's item copies.

model.description: The model row whose copies count; absent to count the whole unit's.

breakpoints.description: The cap is the `choices` of the breakpoint with the largest `models` at or below the unit's model count, or 0 when none is.

per_choice.description: How many times one choice may be taken; absent for no limit.

options.description: The app's wargear widgets: one entry per option it shows on a model row (or for the unit, when `model` is absent), with the item the option adds, its input and its default copies. A checkbox is taken at most once, so a row whose every option for an item is a checkbox carries at most that many copies of it (or its stock copies, when more). A row the default unit has at most one model of, whose stock options are all checkboxes, shows its widgets per model, so its caps scale with its model count.

default.description: Copies of the item the default unit's row takes through this option.

uniform.description: Every model on the row (or in the unit, when `model` is absent) that takes no substitute carries the same main option.

game_modes.description: Game modes this unit composition is legal or authored for; absent implies matched-play.

items.description: A multiset of items: each repo weapon or wargear id with its copy count.
